summary.title: Recursive Synthesis for Long-Horizon Terminal Tasks

details: High-quality long-horizon terminal-agent training tasks require mutually consistent instruction, environment, reference solution, and verifier; human authoring costs hundreds to thousands of dollars per task and direct LLM generation breaks these dependencies.

RST (Recursive Synthetic Terminal Tasks): a recursive, solution-first synthesis loop that takes a verified seed task, extends its executable reference solution via a selected rewrite operator, then realigns verifier, instruction, and environment to the new workflow.

Acceptance requires oracle validity (reference solution passes the private verifier in a fresh sandbox) plus contract validity (every verified requirement is stated in the instruction or discoverable in the workspace); accepted tasks become seeds for the next round, so difficulty compounds recursively.
639 verified bootstrap seeds sampled from TerminalWorld; 15 recursive rounds yielding 37,484 accepted tasks (R1 = 2,820) at ~$0.05 per passed task.
Task bundle = instruction.md, task.toml, environment/Dockerfile, solution/solve.sh, tests/test.sh + test_state.py; generation restricted to these six files.

40 rewrite operators in 5 families, chosen by an affordance scan plus family-balance and inverse-frequency penalties; explicit transformation contract requiring >=4 distinguishable checks including shortcut rejection.

Deterministic gates (>=3 files changed, >=8 changed solution lines, >=12 changed verifier lines, instruction <=180 words and <=1.6x parent length, no private-test leakage), static preflight, then Daytona sandbox oracle run via Harbor with at most two bounded feedback repairs.
Per-round seed selection (~1,000 seeds) under caps on parent lineage (<=4 descendants), category, rewrite family, and source cohort, with lineage-recoverability checks.
Fixed solvers DeepSeek-V4-Pro and GPT-5.6-sol evaluated on matched per-round subsets with pass@4 and partial credit (fraction of verifier checks passed), at 70/80/90% thresholds.
Diversity metrics: domain entropy over 19 consolidated domains, rewrite-family entropy, operator coverage, parent lineage coverage, parent-child novelty, within-round nearest-neighbor similarity.
Leakage audit: normalized 13-token sliding-window match and 5-gram Jaccard against 89 TB2, 100 Terminal-Bench Hard, and 46 LHTB tasks.

SFT on rejection-sampled successful Qwen3.5 rollouts on synthesized tasks; models Qwen3.5-27B and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B; SLIME framework, one epoch on 10,778 examples, global batch 128, context up to 262k, LR 3e-6 to 3e-7, 64 GPUs (TP4/PP2/CP2; MoE variant TP2/PP8/CP2/EP4).
Checkpoints trained on trajectories from one, two, and three recursive synthesis stages to test the effect of additional rounds.

Agentic PPO on Qwen3.5-27B: actor cold-started from base, critic warm-loaded, GAE, clipping eps=0.2, no KL penalty or entropy bonus, whitened advantages, reward from each task's verifier with shaping; training pool = all 37,484 tasks reshuffled per epoch.
Terminal-Bench 2 (89 tasks), Terminal-Bench Hard (100-task subset of TMax-15K), Long-Horizon Terminal Bench (46 tasks, dense partial credit).
Harbor with Terminus-2 agent harness, Daytona sandboxes, SGLang OpenAI-compatible serving; RL results averaged over three evaluation runs; base models and DeepSeek-V4-Pro as comparison points.

key_findings.finding: Recursive verified synthesis scales to fifteen rounds without collapse, producing tens of thousands of executable tasks at negligible cost.
key_findings.evidence: 639 seeds yield 37,484 accepted tasks at ~$0.05 each; passed-task yield per 1,000 seed attempts stays between 498.2 and 572.2 (551.6 at R1, 530.0 at R15) and candidate pass rate stays within 74.5-81.5% (77.5% vs 78.0%).

key_findings.finding: Each round adds genuine executable work rather than longer prompts, and this translates into steep difficulty growth for a fixed solver.
key_findings.evidence: From R1 to R15 median solution length grows 67 to 374 lines, commands 40 to 244, unique CLI tools 17 to 71, verifier assertions 17 to 57, while instruction length grows only 85 to 122 words; DeepSeek-V4-Pro pass@4 falls 90% to 2.5% and mean partial credit 0.970 to 0.170, with failed attempts satisfying >=75% of checks dropping from 86.4% to 1.2%.

key_findings.finding: Training on trajectories from the synthesized tasks improves terminal-agent performance at two model scales, with monotone gains from adding more recursive rounds.
key_findings.evidence: Three-stage SFT lifts Terminal-Bench 2 from 41.2% to 47.9% (27B) and 43.8% to 49.4% (122B-A10B), Terminal-Bench Hard from 22.7% to 28.3% and 20.0% to 30.0%, and LHTB partial credit from 18.1% to 22.4% and 18.9% to 23.6%.

key_findings.finding: Verifier-based PPO on the synthesized task pool gives further gains, largest on independently constructed hard tasks.
key_findings.evidence: Qwen3.5-27B-RL reaches 49.44% (TB2), 32.00% (TB Hard), 22.07% (LHTB), relative gains of 20.0%, 41.2%, 21.9% over base; during training the 5-step moving-average verifier reward rises from ~0.11 to above 0.14 while mean trajectory length grows from ~19-20 to over 30 turns.

key_findings.finding: Recursion preserves diversity and alignment quality instead of degenerating into duplicates or hidden-requirement tasks.
key_findings.evidence: Domain normalized entropy 0.821 to 0.817, rewrite-family entropy 2.26-2.31 bits (max 2.32), 36 of 40 operators present in R15 with top operator only 8.0%; median within-round nearest-neighbor similarity rises 0.223 to 0.464 but stays below 0.5; hidden-check protection rises 38.2% to 63.5% and weakly grounded tasks fall 32.8% to 1.2%; leakage audit finds no benchmark match and max 5-gram Jaccard below 0.009.
